title: Does steering toward 'honesty' actually reduce deception, or just reduce verbalized deception?

original_idea.body: Use a task with separable behavior and explanation channels, steer with an honesty vector, and measure separately verbalized honesty vs actual non-manipulation to test whether steering moves words or deeds.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: tests whether honesty steering changes deeds or only words, bearing on unverbalized-deception threat.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Separable task + honesty steering; careful task design needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable though task construction adds work.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Model-organism deception work labs deprioritize, open models, foundational.

novelty.reasoning: Words-vs-deeds dissociation under honesty steering appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: A fresh angle on honesty steering.
